newsitem.title: USA: New talks seen on IMF lending to Ivory Coast.
newsitem.headline: New talks seen on IMF lending to Ivory Coast.

text.p: Further discussions are planned between the International Monetary Fund and the Ivory Coast on a new three-year loan, but some progress was made in recent talks, an IMF source said on Tuesday.
The source said IMF experts who visited Ivory Coast earlier this month for a donor conference would report back to the IMF board before the next round of talks.
"There has been some progress on structural issues," the source said, highlighting the decision to liberalize commodity trade as one area where changes had been agreed.
"But there are issues that remain on the table and for which another round of discussions will be planned. No date has been set so far."

Donor sources said in Abidjan on Monday that there had been no agreement on a new loan at the conference, but that an IMF lending program could be ready by the end of October, after a range of "micro-managment things" had been sorted out.

The Abidjan sources said the decision to reform the Caistab commodities marketing board had removed one stumbling block to a deal. The reforms will free marketing prices and allow the private sector to take charge of export auctions for coffee and cocoa from 1999.
Ivory Coast, which recorded low-inflation economic growth of seven percent in 1995 and 1996, is viewed as a star reformer by the IMF.
But IMF approval of a new three-year Enhanced Structural Adjustment Program is essential if Ivory Coast is to have a chance of participating in the IMF's Highly Indebted Poor Countries' initiative.
The initiative offers substantial debt relief to heavily indebted developing countries with a strong track record of economic reforms.
